The most important announcement at Dreamforce this week was not a new feature — it was an architectural decision.

Salesforce introduced AIforce and Koa, deliberately separating the AI interface from the trusted enterprise context and execution layer. Koa adds CRM-specific reasoning through a model that Salesforce controls — not a frontier lab. This means the intelligence layer is governed by the platform that holds your customer data and business logic.

HubSpot made a parallel move the same week, launching Growth Context to rebuild its CRM around continuously assembled customer context deployed across marketing, sales, and service. Mistral reinforced the same thesis: enterprise AI is about control, not just intelligence.

Three major vendors converging on one bet. The model is becoming a commodity. The context layer — your proprietary data, business rules, and workflow logic — is where enterprise AI value will accrue.

For CEOs and CTOs, the question is whether your AI architecture gives you control over that context layer or whether you have already ceded it to a vendor's execution framework.
